comments.body:
> @gregtatcam @yinyiqian1 Please review this PR and advise on the next steps.

@ckeshava I don't think this should be "fixed" by failing the transaction — the current outcome is correct; it's the intent that reads unclearly.
AMMClawback is a compliance recovery that deliberately works without holder cooperation: it already withdraws with IgnoreFreeze/IgnoreAuth and recreates deleted MPTokens. Gating the paired-asset return on the holder's reserve reintroduces the holder veto the design intentionally strips out — a holder could block clawback indefinitely by deleting the paired trustline and keeping spendable XRP below one incremental reserve. tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE here is a regression, not the safe choice. And the trustline holds the holder's own returned asset, so failing doesn't protect them — it denies them the asset and blocks the issuer.
That said, the current code does look accidental: std::max(priorBalance, balance) with priorBalance = the issuer's preFeeBalance_ reads like the wrong account was passed. So rather than change behavior, let's make intent explicit:

Skip sufficientReserve on the clawback path (e.g. when authHandling == IgnoreAuth) so the outcome no longer depends on the issuer incidentally holding enough XRP, and
Add a comment noting clawback intentionally bypasses the recipient reserve check, consistent with IgnoreFreeze/IgnoreAuth.

This keeps the correct outcome, removes the ambiguity, and fixes a real edge case: for MPT the check consults the issuer's balance alone, so a low-XRP issuer can currently be blocked.

prs.body:
## Summary

`AMMClawback` reuses `AMMWithdraw`'s helpers to return the paired asset to the holder. When the paired asset's trustline or MPToken has to be auto-created, the holder's owner reserve was checked against `max(issuer pre-fee balance, holder current balance)` — the issuer's balance leaks into the comparison because `sfAccount` on an `AMMClawback` is the issuer. As a result the clawback failed with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE` whenever neither the issuer nor the holder could cover the extra owner reserve, even though clawback is a compliance operation that should not be blocked by a reserve requirement. A holder could also deliberately veto a clawback by deleting the paired trustline/MPToken and keeping a low spendable balance.

## Fix

Gated behind the `fixCleanup3_4_0` amendment. A new `ReserveHandling` enum is threaded through the withdraw helpers: `AMMClawback` passes `ReserveHandling::IgnoreReserve` so the owner-reserve check is skipped, while `AMMWithdraw` passes `ReserveHandling::EnforceReserve` and its behavior is unchanged. Clawback takes precedence over the reserve requirement.

## Tests

`testClawbackBypassesReserve` in `AMMClawback_test` (IOU paired asset) and `AMMClawbackMPT_test` (MPT paired asset) cover both paths:

- amendment enabled → the clawback succeeds and the paired holding is created for the holder, even though neither the issuer nor the holder can cover the extra owner reserve.
- amendment disabled → legacy behavior preserved: the transaction fails with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE` and no paired holding is created.

Both tests also assert that a plain `AMMWithdraw` under the same conditions still fails with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE`, confirming the bypass is scoped to clawback.

## High Level Overview of Change
Fixes an AMMClawback boundary case where a requested clawback amount maps to exactly all of the holder’s LP tokens.



### Context of Change
Previously, AMMClawback::equalWithdrawMatchingOneAmount() only took the full-clawback path when `lpTokensWithdraw > holdLPtokens` If the computed LP token amount was exactly equal to the holder’s LP token balance, the code fell through to the partial-withdraw path, which could fail with `tecAMM_BALANCE` in last-holder rounding scenarios.


### API Impact



- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)

## High Level Overview of Change



### Context of Change
Spec link: https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/discussions/212

This PR includes:
1. Allow AMMCreate for clawback-enabled tokens
    changes are in `AMMCreate` and `AMM_test`
2. AMMDeposit prohibits depositing if either of the paired tokens is frozen
    changes are in `AMMDeposit` and `AMM_test` 
3. Added AMMClawback transaction.
    mainly in `AMMClawback` and `AMMClawback_test`

___________________________________________________________________________
Some refactor happens because I want to call some functions from AMMWithdraw.
**1. Refactor of `withdraw`:**
- Added static `withdraw` function to return the `amountWithdrawActual` and `amount2WithdrawActual` as well.
- private overload `withdraw`.
- Previously in `withdraw` function, it checks `if (!(ctx_.tx[sfFlags] & (tfWithdrawAll | tfOneAssetWithdrawAll)))` to decide if it needs to call `adjustAmountsByLPTokens`. Because these flags only belong to `AMMWithdraw`, to make this function also work for AMMClawback, I changed it by passing enum WithdrawAll.

**2. Refactor of `equalWithdrawTokens`:**
  Because I want to call this function in `AMMClawback`, I make a public static `equalWithdrawTokens` function. And also private overload `equalWithdrawTokens`

**3. Added `deleteAMMAccountIfEmpty`**
  Since I need to reuse the logic in AMMWithdraw that when all the tokens are withdrawn, the amm account is deleted, so I added function `deleteAMMAccountIfEmpty`.

___________________________________________________________________________
**Reason of adding flag `tfClawTwoAssets`:**
If the issuer issues both assets `A` and `B` in the amm pool, when clawing back `A`, `tfClawTwoAssets` is used to decide if the paired token `B` to be clawed back as well or goes back to the holder. If  tfClawTwoAssets` is set true, the paired token will be clawed back as well. Otherwise, the paired token goes back to the holder.

**Reason of adding both `asset` and `amount` in the `AMMClawback` request:**
`amount` is used to decide if the issuer wants to clawback all the tokens or not. (if `amount` is not provided, then clawback all)  Imagine if an issuer issues both asset `A` and `B` in the amm pool, and the issuer wants to clawback all `A` and give back all the corresponding `B` to the holder. Then the issuer just needs to specify `A` in `asset` field and leave out `amount` field.

**Reasons for setting tfee as 0:**
Because we are doing a two-asset withdrawal. tfee is not used.

**Reasons for using asset1 and asset2 to navigate amm**
To keep the same with other amm transactions and make it simple.
So we require providing asset1 and asset2 in the AMMClawback request.

issues.author: mvadari
issues.body:
**Severity**: LOW

**Feature**: Clawback (cross-cutting)

##### AMMClawback preclaim missing holder LP token balance check

**Severity**: LOW

AMMClawback::preclaim() verifies the AMM exists, the issuer has clawback flags, and the holder account exists, but does NOT check if the holder has any LP tokens in the AMM. The LP token balance check only happens in applyGuts(), returning tecAMM\_BALANCE. Fee is charged but no clawback occurs.

**Root cause**: AMMClawback::preclaim() at lines 70-98 checks AMM existence and clawback flags but omits an ammLPHolds check.

src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/dex/AMMClawback.cpp:70-98

**Exploit scenario**: 1. Issuer submits AMMClawback targeting a holder with no LP tokens. 2. Preclaim passes. 3. applyGuts returns tecAMM\_BALANCE. 4. Fee is charged.

**Financial impact**: Fee loss for submitter. No fund theft.

**Suggested fix**: Add LP token balance check in preclaim.

issues.title: AMMClawback preclaim returns tesSUCCESS instead of tecNO_PERMISSION for unauthorized clawback
issues.author: hgandhi-rx
issues.body:
## Summary

AMMClawback preclaim returns tesSUCCESS instead of tecNO_PERMISSION for unauthorized clawback.

## Details

In AMMClawback::preclaim, when featureMPTokensV2 is NOT enabled, if the issuer does NOT have the AllowTrustLineClawback flag set or HAS the NoFreeze flag set, the function returns tesSUCCESS instead of tecNO_PERMISSION. The comment on line 104-105 explicitly says 'return no permission' but the code returns success. This causes the transaction to proceed through doApply, which performs the actual clawback by: (1) withdrawing the holder's LP token position from the AMM pool, (2) transferring the withdrawn assets from the holder to the issuer via directSendNoFee. The original code (before MPTokensV2 refactoring) correctly returned tecNO_PERMISSION. The refactoring introduced tesSUCCESS by mistake. Comparing with Clawback.cpp (line 92-95) and VaultClawback.cpp (lines 192-199), which both correctly return tecNO_PERMISSION for the same check, confirms this is a bug.

**Root cause**: Line 108 in AMMClawback.cpp returns tesSUCCESS where it should return tecNO_PERMISSION. This causes the preclaim to pass when the issuer lacks clawback authorization, allowing doApply to execute the unauthorized clawback. The early return at line 108 also skips the subsequent checkClawAsset validation (lines 111-134) that would correctly return tecNO_PERMISSION.

`src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/dex/AMMClawback.cpp:101-109`
```cpp
std::uint32_t const issuerFlagsIn = sleIssuer->getFieldU32(sfFlags);
if (!ctx.view.rules().enabled(featureMPTokensV2))
{
    // If AllowTrustLineClawback is not set or NoFreeze is set, return no
    // permission
    if (((issuerFlagsIn & lsfAllowTrustLineClawback) == 0u) ||
        ((issuerFlagsIn & lsfNoFreeze) != 0u))
        return tesSUCCESS;
}
```

**Exploit scenario**: 1. An AMM pool exists for IOU_A/XRP where IOU_A issuer does NOT have AllowTrustLineClawback flag set.
2. featureAMMClawback is enabled but featureMPTokensV2 is NOT yet enabled.
3. Alice has deposited into this AMM pool and holds LP tokens worth significant value.
4. The IOU_A issuer submits an AMMClawback transaction targeting Alice's LP position.
5. Preclaim at line 106-108 checks: issuer does NOT have AllowTrustLineClawback → condition is true → returns tesSUCCESS (bug!).
6. doApply executes applyGuts which: (a) withdraws Alice's entire LP position from the AMM (burning her LP tokens, sending IOU_A and XRP to Alice), (b) transfers IOU_A from Alice to the issuer via directSendNoFee.
7. Result: The issuer successfully claws back IOU_A from Alice's AMM position without ever having AllowTrustLineClawback permission.

**Financial impact**: Attacker (any IOU issuer) can steal the full value of any holder's LP position in AMM pools containing their issued token. The stolen amount equals the holder's proportional share of the issuer's asset in the pool. For large pools this could be millions of tokens.

**Invariant gap**: No invariant checks clawback authorization. The ValidAMM invariant checker only validates mathematical properties (sqrt(A*B) >= LP), not authorization.

**Suggested fix**: Change line 108 from 'return tesSUCCESS;' to 'return tecNO_PERMISSION;' to match the comment and the pattern used in Clawback.cpp and VaultClawback.cpp.

---

## Impact

Branch: [`ripple/attackathon-april-2026`](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/tree/ripple/attackathon-april-2026)

issues.title: [XLS-73] Incorrect error in AMMClawback: temINVALID_FLAG returned instead of temMALFORMED
issues.author: HugoDowsers
issues.body:
**Issue Description**

While validating an AMMClawback transaction, if a transaction contains both an incorrect asset issuer (Asset.issuer) and an invalid usage of the tfClawTwoAssets flag, the system returns temINVALID_FLAG instead of temMALFORMED.

XLS-73 specifies that failing the tfClawTwoAssets validation (when the second asset is not issued by the sender) should return tecNO_PERMISSION rather than temINVALID_FLAG.

https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/0a626d95f435f603b89ba5bf95fe201c71088e7a/src/xrpld/app/tx/detail/AMMClawback.cpp#L48
https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0073-amm-clawback

**Steps to Reproduce**

- Submit an AMMClawback transaction where the Account field (the sender) does not match the issuer defined in the Asset field (Violation of Rule S2).
- Simultaneously enable the tfClawTwoAssets flag while the second asset (Asset2) is issued by a third party or is XRP (Violation of Rule S3).


**Expected Result**

The transaction should return temMALFORMED. The failure to validate the primary asset's issuer (Asset.issuer == Account) is an error that must be detected before any secondary flag analysis is performed.

**Actual Result**

The transaction returns temINVALID_FLAG. The current code in AMMClawback::preflight evaluates the condition (flags & tfClawTwoAssets && asset.account != asset2.account) before the mandatory check (asset.account != issuer).

**Environment**

   OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
    Compiler: GCC 11 / Clang 14
    Boost: 1.77+
    Version: xrpld develop branch (post XLS-73 integration)

**Supporting Files**

None.
